_about: Texts written by the build session (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5, acting as the model) from dashboard/facts/W<wk>.json and W<wk>_cards.json ONLY, using the SYSTEM_SUMMARY / SYSTEM_CARD prompts in 16_generate_summaries.py. facts_md5 records the facts version each text was written from; 16 ignores a text whose facts changed. Every number is re-checked by 17_validate_summaries.py.

23.text: Three retention warnings open the period. Returning customers were flat at 159 vs 159, returning Gen Z fell to 17 from 26 (-34.6%), and only 4.5% of new Gen Z joined Insider. W23 is the first week in the extract, so L4W and period-to-date equal this one week and the inventory rules stay off until the four-week window fills. Demand grew +14.4% YoY to $70.0K (LY $61.2K), with transactions +6.6% and AOV +7.3% at $311.32. Gen Z new customers were 22 vs 15 (+46.7%), 33.3% of all new customers vs 28.8% last year. Tabby led growth with +10.5 pts of contribution (+70.8% YoY), while Trench was the largest drag at -3.0 pts (-67.9%). Trench also shows 32.5 weeks of supply on a one-week sales window, a watch item rather than an alert.

24.text: Transactions fell -2.9% YoY in W24, but demand still grew +9.1% to $75.2K because AOV rose +12.4% to $321.57, so this was a basket week, not a traffic week. The retention proxies stayed weak over W23–W24: returning customers -2.7%, returning Gen Z 36 vs 51 (-29.4%), and only 16.3% of new Gen Z joined Insider. Gen Z new customers were 21 vs 16 (+31.3%), 32.8% of new customers vs 25.8% last year. Demand is +7.4% WoW and +11.6% period-to-date. Tabby added +14.1 pts of growth (+109%), while Tailored Jacket was the biggest drag (-3.0 pts, -63.3%) and holds 22.4 weeks of supply. Tabby cover is down to 5.1 weeks vs 11.4 LY on a sales window that is still truncated, so no stock rule fires yet.

25.text: Demand fell -16.4% WoW in W25, and this time it is traffic: transactions -12.8% WoW while AOV slipped only -4.1%. Against last year the week still grew +8.3% ($62.9K vs $58.1K), and period-to-date demand is +10.6%. Retention proxies remain the weak spot over W23–W25: returning customers -5.1% (463 vs 488), returning Gen Z 49 vs 67 (-26.9%), and new Gen Z Insider attach 19.4%. Acquisition is the bright spot: 29 Gen Z new customers vs 12 (+142%), 41.4% of all new vs 24.0% LY. Tabby (+11.9 pts, +75.2%) and Pillow Tabby (+4.1 pts, +172%) carry the growth, while Tailored Jacket is -59.5%. Tabby cover is already 4.5 weeks vs 9.6 LY, though the window is still truncated, so there is no stock alert yet.

26.text: W26 is the first week the inventory rules can fire, and Tabby already has 3.9 weeks of supply vs 8.4 last year, less than half. At the other end, Tailored Jacket holds 25.9 weeks (LY 6.4) and Trench 17.9 (LY 8.0), while L4W demand is -56.3% for Tailored Jacket, -40.2% for Knit Dress and -35.8% for Loafer. Demand was +4.2% YoY at $74.8K and +18.9% WoW, a traffic-led rebound (transactions +29.4% WoW, AOV -8.1%). L4W demand is +8.8%. Gen Z new customers were 26 vs 17 (+52.9%), 32.1% of new vs 28.8% LY, and 98 vs 60 over L4W (+63.3%). Retention proxies are still negative: returning customers -1.8% (646 vs 658), returning Gen Z 77 vs 87 (-11.5%), and new Gen Z Insider attach 19.4%.

27.text: Tabby's cover kept shrinking in W27: 3.5 weeks of supply against 7.4 last year, and Pillow Tabby is next lowest at 4.4 (LY 7.6). Demand grew +12.9% YoY to $76.9K, with transactions +11.2% doing the work and AOV +1.6%. Gen Z new customers reached 34 vs 12 (+183%), 41.5% of new vs 17.4% LY; over L4W it is 110 vs 57 (+93.0%). Halo is the drag: over L4W Rogue is -36.8%, Tailored Jacket -55.9%, Knit Dress -45.6% and Loafer -37.2%, while Tailored Jacket still holds 25.3 weeks of supply and Trench 18.5. Retention stays flat: returning customers 654 vs 654, returning Gen Z 80 vs 87 (-8.0%), and new Gen Z Insider attach 18.2%. L4W demand is +8.6% and period-to-date +9.7%.

28.text: Tabby and Pillow Tabby are now critically low on stock: 2.5 and 2.8 weeks of supply against 6.7 and 7.8 last year, with 116 and 41 units on hand. Both are G3 winners and Gen Z gateways, so a stock-out would cap the main growth engine. Demand jumped +23.1% YoY to $87.8K (+14.2% WoW), but mostly on basket: AOV +13.0% at $343.16 vs $303.72, transactions +8.9%. Gen Z new customers were 39 vs 15 (+160%), 43.3% of new vs 22.7% LY. Over L4W, Rogue is -44.6%, Knit Dress -62.6% and Loafer -32.5%, and Knit Dress sits on 21.2 weeks of supply (LY 8.6). Retention: returning customers +0.9% (650 vs 644), returning Gen Z 81 vs 85 (-4.7%), and new Gen Z Insider attach 18.0%.

29.text: Pillow Tabby is down to 1.8 weeks of supply and Tabby to 2.1, against 5.1 and 7.0 last year, with only 27 and 92 units left. These are the period's growth leaders, so stock is the decision this week. Demand was +12.7% YoY ($71.3K vs $63.3K) on transactions +14.7%. The -18.8% WoW drop is basket, not traffic: transactions -2.3% WoW and AOV -16.9% after the W28 spike. L4W demand is +13.2% and period-to-date +12.1%. Gen Z new customers were 41 vs 16 (+156%), 47.1% of new vs 27.6% LY, and 140 vs 60 over L4W (+133%). But only 16.4% of new Gen Z joined Insider over L4W. Halo apparel is the drag: Knit Dress -62.7% and Rogue -35.9% over L4W, with Knit Dress holding 20.7 weeks of supply.

30.text: Replenishment has stopped following demand: over W24–W29 Tabby received stock equal to 28% of units sold (LY 95%) and Pillow Tabby 29% (LY 85%). The latest snapshot shows Tabby at 1.9 weeks of supply (LY 7.5) with 82 units, and Pillow Tabby at 1.6 (LY 5.1) with 24. W30 is a partial week (Sun–Wed, 4 days), compared with the same 4 days last year: demand +21.7% YoY ($44.9K vs $36.9K), transactions +11.4%, AOV +9.3%. Gen Z took 56.0% of new customers (28 vs 5 LY), and L4W Gen Z new is 142 vs 48 (+196%). Only 15.5% of new Gen Z joined Insider over L4W. Knit Dress (21.2 weeks of supply, -60.3% L4W demand) and Trench (16.9) carry the overstock. Like-for-like period-to-date demand is +12.8%.

stock.headline: Tabby opens the period with 6.7 weeks of supply against 10.3 last year.
stock.body: This reading uses a 1-week sales window, so the inventory rules stay off until the window is full. Pillow Tabby shows 17.8 weeks (LY 12.6) on a single week of sales; read both as early signals, not alerts.

retention.headline: Returning customers were flat at 159 vs 159, and returning Gen Z fell to 17 from 26.
retention.body: That is -34.6% for returning Gen Z, and only 4.5% of new Gen Z joined Insider (LY 26.7%). This is a mix proxy (D8): CUST_ID can't link buyers across years, so read it as a direction, not a cohort rate.

pattern.headline: Gen Z is 33.3% of new customers in the first week, up from 28.8% last year.
pattern.body: That is 22 Gen Z new customers vs 15. One week isn't a trend yet; I'll track the share week by week.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers are up +46.7% in the first week, 22 vs 15.
win.body: Tabby drives the start: +70.8% YoY and +10.5 pts of growth on its own. Total demand is +14.4%.

overstock.headline: Trench holds 32.5 weeks of supply against 6.7 last year.
overstock.body: That reading rests on a single week of sales, so it is a watch item, not an alert. Tailored Jacket is at 23.8 weeks (LY 6.6).

stock.headline: Tabby cover has fallen to 5.1 weeks, less than half of last year's 11.4.
stock.body: The sales window is still only 2 weeks, so no rule fires yet. Tabby holds 246 units; Pillow Tabby looks comfortable at 11.2 weeks (LY 10.7).

retention.headline: Returning customers are -2.7% YoY over W23–W24, and returning Gen Z is down to 36 from 51.
retention.body: Returning Gen Z is -29.4% and new Gen Z Insider attach is 16.3% vs 29.0% LY, so last year's Gen Z buyers aren't visibly coming back. Insider enrolment at the first purchase is the lever to test.

pattern.headline: Gen Z took 32.8% of new customers in W24, close to the 33.3% of the first week.
pattern.body: Last year the same week was 25.8%. Weekly counts are small (21 Gen Z new), so a one-point move is noise.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers are up +38.7% over W23–W24, 43 vs 31.
win.body: Tabby more than doubled (+109% over L4W) and added +14.1 pts of growth. Demand is +11.6% period-to-date.

overstock.headline: Tailored Jacket holds 22.4 weeks of supply against 5.3 last year.
overstock.body: Trench is at 17.3 weeks (LY 6.8). The sales window is still truncated, so treat these as early signs of a Halo apparel overhang.

stock.headline: Tabby is down to 4.5 weeks of supply and Pillow Tabby to 6.6, against 9.6 and 13.4 last year.
stock.body: With 213 Tabby units on hand and a 3-week sales window, this is the trend the stock rules will judge once the window is full in W26.

retention.headline: Returning customers fell -5.1% (463 vs 488) and returning Gen Z -26.9% over W23–W25.
retention.body: Only 19.4% of new Gen Z joined Insider vs 27.9% LY, while 21.0% of all new customers did. Without a loyalty hook, the Gen Z acquisition wave won't show up as returning demand.

pattern.headline: Gen Z share of new customers rose to 41.4%, from 33.3% in W23.
pattern.body: Last year this week was 24.0%. 29 Gen Z customers were new this week, the momentum the acquisition goal is after.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers are up +67.4% period-to-date: 72 vs 43.
win.body: Tabby (+75.2%, +11.9 pts) and Pillow Tabby (+172%, +4.1 pts) lead L4W growth. Gen Z is 36.0% of new customers vs 26.2% LY.

overstock.headline: Tailored Jacket is at 22.7 weeks of supply and Trench at 18.6, against 5.1 and 8.6 last year.
overstock.body: Apparel stock is building while its demand isn't. These become rule-checked once the four-week window fills in W26.

stock.headline: Tabby has 3.9 weeks of supply, less than half of last year's 8.4.
stock.body: W26 is the first week with a full four-week window, and the WOS-collapse rule fires for Tabby (183 units on hand). Pillow Tabby is at 6.3 weeks vs 12.2 LY. Check inbound Tabby supply now; it is the main growth family.

retention.headline: Returning Gen Z is down to 77 from 87 (-11.5%) over the first four weeks.
retention.body: All returning customers are -1.8% (646 vs 658). Insider attach of new Gen Z is 19.4% vs 23.3% LY, about level with all new customers at 19.6%.

pattern.headline: Gen Z share of new customers dipped to 32.1% in W26.
pattern.body: It is still above last year's 28.8% and in line with the first week's 33.3%, on 26 new Gen Z customers vs 17 LY.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers are up +63.3% period-to-date, 98 vs 60.
win.body: Gen Z share of new is 34.9% vs 26.9% LY. Tabby (+56.8%) and Pillow Tabby (+125%) add +9.6 and +3.3 pts of L4W growth, while total L4W demand is +8.8%.

overstock.headline: Tailored Jacket has 25.9 weeks of supply while its demand is -56.3% over L4W.
overstock.body: Trench holds 17.9 weeks (LY 8.0) and Knit Dress demand is -40.2%. Slow Halo apparel is tying up stock that the Tabby franchise needs; plan markdowns or transfers.

stock.headline: Tabby is at 3.5 weeks of supply and Pillow Tabby at 4.4, versus 7.4 and 7.6 last year.
stock.body: Cover keeps shrinking while demand grows: Tabby is down to 160 units and Pillow Tabby to 55. If cover keeps falling, the low-stock rule escalates to critical because both are G3 winners and Gen Z gateways.

retention.headline: Returning customers are flat at 654 vs 654, and returning Gen Z is -8.0% over L4W.
retention.body: Period-to-date returning Gen Z is 97 vs 113 (-14.2%). New Gen Z Insider attach is 18.2% vs 24.6% LY, the gap that R3 targets.

pattern.headline: Gen Z share of new customers is back up to 41.5% in W27, against 17.4% last year.
pattern.body: The W23 starting point was 33.3%. This week 34 Gen Z customers were new vs 12 LY.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers are up +83.3% period-to-date, 132 vs 72.
win.body: Gen Z is 36.4% of new customers vs 24.7% LY. Tabby (+36.8%, +6.8 pts) and Pillow Tabby (+84.6%, +3.3 pts) lead L4W growth.

overstock.headline: Tailored Jacket holds 25.3 weeks of supply and Trench 18.5, against 6.9 and 8.0 last year.
overstock.body: Demand keeps falling over L4W: Tailored Jacket -55.9%, Knit Dress -45.6%, Rogue -36.8% and Loafer -37.2%. Shift open-to-buy from Halo apparel toward Hero.

stock.headline: Tabby and Pillow Tabby are down to 2.5 and 2.8 weeks of supply, against 6.7 and 7.8 last year.
stock.body: Both families are now in critical low stock, with 116 and 41 units left, and both are G3 winners and the Gen Z gateway. Open the inventory view and confirm inbound supply for Tabby first.

retention.headline: Returning customers grew only +0.9% over L4W, and returning Gen Z fell to 81 from 85.
retention.body: Period-to-date returning Gen Z is -14.0% (117 vs 136). Only 18.0% of new Gen Z joined Insider in L4W vs 21.4% last year.

pattern.headline: Gen Z share of new customers reached 43.3% in W28, up from 33.3% in W23.
pattern.body: Last year's W28 was 22.7%, and 39 Gen Z customers were new vs 15.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers nearly doubled period-to-date: 171 vs 87 (+96.6%).
win.body: Gen Z is 37.7% of new customers vs 24.3% LY. Pillow Tabby (+133%) and Tabby (+27.1%) add +5.0 and +5.5 pts of L4W growth; total L4W demand is +12.3%.

overstock.headline: Knit Dress has 21.2 weeks of supply while its L4W demand is -62.6%.
overstock.body: Trench (16.5, LY 7.8) and Tailored Jacket (15.6, LY 8.0) are also over the high-stock line, and Rogue demand is -44.6%. Clear the apparel overhang before buying more.

stock.headline: Tabby has 2.1 weeks of supply and Pillow Tabby 1.8, while replenishment covered only 28% of what Tabby sold.
stock.body: Last year the same week held 7.0 and 5.1 weeks, and Tabby receipts covered 95% of sales. At this pace Tabby runs out in about 2.6 weeks and Pillow Tabby in 2.2, putting $23.1K of sample demand at risk (7.7% of the next four weeks). Re-open replenishment on both now (R1).

retention.headline: Only 16.4% of new Gen Z joined Insider over L4W, the gap behind a flat returning base.
retention.body: Period-to-date returning customers are 1,142 vs 1,142 and returning Gen Z is -6.5%, even though L4W improved (+3.8%). The gap is widest in Outlet (9.7% vs 23.1% for other new customers) and Greater China (5.1% vs 21.7%). Enrol at the first Gen Z purchase: +10% returning Gen Z is worth about 0.85% of demand (R3).

pattern.headline: Gen Z share of new customers climbed to 47.1% in W29, up from 33.3% in W23.
pattern.body: Last year the same week was 27.6%. 41 Gen Z customers were new vs 16 LY; find out what drove it, because the extract can't explain it.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers have more than doubled period-to-date: 212 vs 103 (+106%).
win.body: Gen Z is 39.3% of new customers vs 24.8% LY. Tabby (+26.9%, +5.0 pts) and Pillow Tabby (+60.3%, +3.2 pts) lead L4W growth, so the Tabby franchise is the template to share across the business.

overstock.headline: Knit Dress, Trench and Tailored Jacket hold 20.7, 16.2 and 15.2 weeks of supply against a median of 7.9.
overstock.body: That is 198 units, about $50.5K at retail, above median cover. Knit Dress demand is -62.7% over L4W and Rogue -35.9%; move that open-to-buy to Hero (R2).

stock.headline: Tabby is down to 1.9 weeks of supply and Pillow Tabby to 1.6, after receipts covered only 28% and 29% of units sold.
stock.body: Last year the same snapshot held 7.5 and 5.1 weeks, with receipts at 95% and 85% of sales. Only 82 Tabby and 24 Pillow Tabby units remain; at the current pace the 4-week demand at risk is $23.1K, 7.7% of the next four weeks. Re-open replenishment now (R1).

retention.headline: Insider attach of new Gen Z is 15.5% over L4W, against 23.4% for new Millennials.
retention.body: Period-to-date returning customers are flat (1,239 vs 1,236) and returning Gen Z is -3.1%. The gap sits in Outlet (9.7% vs 23.1%), eComm (12.7% vs 19.2%) and Greater China (5.1% vs 21.7%), so start Insider enrolment there (R3).

pattern.headline: Gen Z took 56.0% of new customers in the first four days of W30, up from 33.3% in W23.
pattern.body: Last year the same four days were at 13.2%, on 28 Gen Z new vs 5. It's a partial week with small counts, but the direction matches the columns above.

win.headline: Gen Z new customers are up +122% like-for-like: 240 vs 108.
win.body: Gen Z is 40.7% of new customers vs 23.8% LY. Over L4W, Tabby (+28.9%, +5.3 pts) and Pillow Tabby (+62.0%, +3.5 pts) lead the franchise, and total demand is +12.8% period-to-date.

overstock.headline: Knit Dress holds 21.2 weeks of supply, Trench 16.9 and Tailored Jacket 16.3, against a median of 7.9.
overstock.body: Together that's 198 units and $50.5K at retail above median cover, while Knit Dress demand is -60.3% over L4W. Mark down or transfer, and move the open-to-buy to Hero (R2).
